scope: DUT build cache, historical source checkouts and orphaned generated RTL under .cache/ after the toolchain upgrade to toffee 2.3.0 / xcomm 2.0.0 / picker 3.0.0.
process_check: No active ucv build/prepare/run or simulation process before deletion; root regression had passed on the new lock.
reason: The DUT cache key includes dependencies/versions.json, so every pre-upgrade DUT package is unreachable by the current lock and cannot support a new-toolchain claim. Historical source checkouts and generated RTL for public baselines are re-obtainable from upstream, and the retained generated RTL keeps DUT rebuilds from requiring a Chisel regeneration.

recovery.dut_packages: ucv build per DUT; closures are copied from the retained generated RTL
recovery.public-893e1580b: git checkout 893e1580b705 from https://github.com/OpenXiangShan/XiangShan.git (no design patches); its generated RTL is gone and must be regenerated
recovery.public-a0c2a26cb: git checkout a0c2a26cbe3c from upstream, or seed from the retained .cache/mirrors/public-a0c2a26cb; its generated RTL must be regenerated

unavailable_after_deletion: .cache/duts packages built against xcomm ABI 3: their build.json receipts and smoke logs are gone, so those runs can no longer be inspected as artifacts. Their conclusions remain only in the committed reports that cited them.
generated RTL for public-893e1580b and public-a0c2a26cb: reproducing a build on those baselines now requires running the Chisel generation again (hours, plus network and 64G heap).

The per-DUT links under suites/*/rtl and suites/*/dut were removed with the deleted packages. Suites that read generated RTL or DUT metadata directly (for example the BPU local-guard and scoreboard controls) now fail with a missing-file error until ucv prepare / ucv build recreates them. This is the same state as a fresh clone and is not a change in their verdicts.
evidence_boundary: Only rebuildable or re-obtainable generated state was removed. No committed report, verdict, bug record or hash index was modified; earlier conclusions keep their original baseline and date, and none of them becomes a new-toolchain result.
